claims.claim_text: The indexed Emrich Nicholson is a probable match to the designer documented by the Museum of Modern Art in 1941.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The distinctive exact name appears in a contemporaneous institutional catalogue with a detailed prewar design chronology.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable. The name is distinctive and contemporaneous, but the catalogue has no OSS reference or archival identifier bridge.
claims.temporal_assessment: The design work is explicitly dated 1936-41; its relation to OSS accession remains unknown.
claims.match_notes: The personnel file is required before the affiliations enter default verified analytics.

claims.claim_text: A probable identity match places Emrich Nicholson as Otto Kuhler's chief designer from 1936 through 1938.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Museum of Modern Art catalogue supplies the role and year-bounded employment chronology.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable because the distinctive name and dates align, but the source does not mention OSS.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar employment; not shown to be immediately pre-OSS.
claims.match_notes: Excluded from default verified-affiliation analytics pending personnel-file confirmation.

claims.claim_text: A probable identity match places Emrich Nicholson in freelance design work from 1938 through at least 1941.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The 1941 catalogue describes Nicholson as a freelance designer associated with Douglas Maier in New York City.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable because the distinctive name and contemporaneous chronology align, but the source does not mention OSS.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar self-employment; the transition to OSS and any intervening role are unknown.
claims.match_notes: Not labeled the immediate or last civilian affiliation without a direct chronology bridge.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Harry G Nickles is confirmed as the USNR lieutenant documented in a wartime OSS security report.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Lt. Harry G. Nickles, USNR, Security Officer for Istanbul
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A direct OSS report identifies Harry G. Nickles by exact name, naval rank, and Istanbul security assignment.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by an exact distinctive name and compatible commissioned naval rank in a direct OSS record.
claims.temporal_assessment: The report documents an OSS wartime assignment, not the person's pre-OSS employer.
claims.match_notes: The index category is corrected to commissioned naval officer; no pre-OSS employment is inferred from the OSS assignment.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Gaspare Nicotri is a high-confidence match to the Italian exile, lawyer, educator, and writer documented in institutional and OSS-related sources.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The distinctive exact name, contemporaneous authorship, and source-attributed accounts of 1942 meetings about assisting OSS converge on one person.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from a distinctive exact name, dated institutional records, and an independent OSS-context bridge.
claims.temporal_assessment: The sources document prewar and 1942 activity but do not name a last civilian employer or exact OSS accession date.
claims.match_notes: The personnel file remains necessary to establish formal OSS status and immediate predecessor affiliation.

claims.claim_text: Gaspare Nicotri was documented as a lawyer, educator, sociologist, and writer before his OSS-related wartime activity.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Queens College's collection description identifies his legal, educational, and sociological work; Turin preserves a dated 1940 article under his name.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence for the distinctive exact-name identity documented across institutional collections.
claims.temporal_assessment: The legal career predates his 1926 exile; the dated article is explicitly pre-OSS, but neither source names an immediate employer.
claims.match_notes: Occupation is kept separate from employer; private practice is not inferred without explicit evidence.

claims.claim_text: Gaspare Nicotri authored an article published in La Parola on 21 September 1940.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The University of Turin archival record identifies the periodical, article title, author, and publication date.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence for the distinctive exact-name match corroborated by other institutional records.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicitly documented prewar authorship; not established as employment or an immediate pre-OSS affiliation.
claims.match_notes: Modeled as a professional affiliation only; the site does not call La Parola his employer.
